page.layout: One printed page of running text in the centre, with a narrow column of text cut off at the right edge (the facing page, partly visible, is not transcribed beyond its fragments). No marginal notes on the left. The digitiser's banner at the foot is omitted.

main_text.p: tiam animo laborent: nihilominus tamen pauca homini, ex maledictis confuto, repofui, attendens illud, quod sapiēter non orator tantum, sed &Philosophus Romanus Cicero inquit: Dissenti-entium inter sereprehen-siones non sunt vitupe-randæ. Maledicta, contumeliæ, tum iracundiæ, contentionesque in dis-putan-

page.notes: The facing page is cut off at the right edge; only fragments are legible there (vide, me, rius, fum, lect, Verl, circ, Cur, cum, qvi) and are not transcribed. The right-hand text is partly obscured by show-through. Line "tiam animo laborent" reads as printed with "tiam" split from "animo" by spacing. The word "putan-" at the foot is a catchword-like broken word continuing on the next page; it is kept in the text as printed.
